premises.rationale: E-06 shows a uniform 2.0h delay across all 6 slots, reinforcing that carrier pickup timing is a modest, flat contributor rather than the dominant mechanism, consistent with the root premise's framing.

output.rationale: E-06 only extends the pickup-log baseline, confirming the E-01 median is a flat, uniform 2.0h figure across all sampled slots rather than slot-dependent or variable. It reinforces the premises that already characterize carrier pickup delay as modest/minor and does not address or contradict any part of the RELEASE-BATCH causal chain, which remains untouched by this evidence.

checks.name: conflict_resolution_tracking
checks.detail: Conflicts C-1 through C-5 on late_shipments.root_cause remain OPEN even though the underlying hypothesis contest already resolved the question (H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE CONFIRMED, others REJECTED); this is a stale bookkeeping gap rather than a substantive inconsistency in the released design.

output.summary: The initial request (SH-CX) was a customer-facing chatbot explaining parcel lateness (CL-01), and logistics lead SH-LOG separately claimed the carrier's 2-hour pickup delay was the cause (CL-02); both claims were tested against evidence and contradicted. The established root problem (PD-1) is that the warehouse RELEASE-BATCH job fails at a high rate (21 of 30 runs, E-04), releasing 290 orders only after the carrier had already picked up, which drives most of the 30% handover-stage lateness (E-02); carrier pickup timing is only a modest 2.0h median delay (E-01, confirmed uniform across slots in E-06) and is not the dominant cause. The system released monitoring/cross-check capability over this confirmed finding (DA-WMS, DA-ORD, DA-PICK) under decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, with no holds, while the specific defect inside RELEASE-BATCH remains undiagnosed and deferred.
key_points: Problem established via competing stakeholder claims: SH-CX wanted a chatbot (CL-01, customer_communication_gap) and SH-LOG blamed carrier pickup delay (CL-02, pickup_delay); both were CONTRADICTED by evidence.

Hypothesis testing confirmed H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE (supported by E-04: 21/30 runs failed, 290 orders released after pickup) as the CRITICAL, confirmed cause, while H-COMMUNICATION-GAP, H-DATA-VISIBILITY-GAP and H-PICKUP-SCHEDULE-FRICTION were REJECTED.

Carrier pickup delay is modest and consistent: median 2.0h across 60 pickups (E-01) and uniform 2.0h across all 6 sampled slots (E-06), ruling it out as the dominant mechanism per assumption A-CARRIER-DELAY-MINOR-CONTRIBU.

Released scope (SD-1): monitor_release_batch_job on DA-WMS, cross_check_late_handover_orders on DA-ORD, and verify_pickup_delay_baseline on DA-PICK; the pickup-delay baseline work item (W-WI-1) is DONE, the other two are PENDING.
A proposed remedy assigns SH-WMS as accountable owner of RELEASE-BATCH with a remediation SLA (SR-OWNERSHIP-RELEASE-BATCH), though this does not remove the root cause.

The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the critical unknown of what specifically causes RELEASE-BATCH to fail (U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE) into VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, whose blocking_scope (diagnosing the defect) sits outside this release's scope.

The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, meaning the monitoring/cross-check capability ships now while the undiagnosed defect and data-completeness questions are tracked as open obligations rather than blockers.
limitations_explained: Completeness of DA-ORD, DA-WMS and DA-PICK is recorded as UNKNOWN (U-DATA-COMPLETENESS), so the measured rates (30% handover lateness, 2h median pickup delay, 21/30 batch failures) may not represent true volumes; VOB-R-2 requires this be resolved before production use, though it did not block this release.

The release does not diagnose the specific defect (code/config/access) causing RELEASE-BATCH to fail; that diagnostic work is blocked by the still-open, HIGH-impact VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, required before release but with its blocking_scope outside what was released.

Whether the Shop-to-Carrier handoff (H-PICK) itself has semantic-validity or delivery problems remains unresolved (U-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-VALIDITY); this question is outside the current monitoring scope, and H-HANDOFF-FAILURE remains an open CANDIDATE hypothesis rather than confirmed or rejected.

The DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, not a full pass; deferred items were converted into tracked verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved, which is why the release carries explicit known limitations instead of being unconditional.
